title: Next.js
description: The React framework for production: App Router, Server Components, rendering strategies and API routes.

renderizacao.title: Rendering
renderizacao.description: Where and when each page is generated.

dados-e-api.title: Data and API routes
dados-e-api.description: Fetching and changing data, and exposing endpoints.

perguntas-de-entrevista.title: Interview questions
perguntas-de-entrevista.description: Next.js questions that often come up in interviews, with a model answer.

app-router.definition: The Next.js routing system based on the app/ folder: each folder is a URL segment and the page.js file inside it is the page. It uses Server Components by default and replaces the old Pages Router (the pages/ folder).

layout.definition: A layout.js file that wraps the pages of a segment and its children (menu, footer). When navigating between child pages, the layout is not unmounted: its state is kept.

rota-dinamica.definition: A segment in brackets, like app/products/[id]/page.js, that matches any value in that position (/products/42). The value reaches the page in params.

arquivos-especiais.definition: Conventional files for each segment: loading.js shows a skeleton while the page loads (via Suspense), error.js catches errors in that part without taking down the app and not-found.js shows when notFound() is called or the route does not exist.

pagina-dinamica.title: Page with a parameter
pagina-dinamica.body: An async Server Component that reads the id from the URL, fetches the product and calls notFound() if it does not exist. In recent versions, params is a Promise.

link-navegacao.title: Navigation with Link
link-navegacao.body: Link navigates without reloading the page and prefetches the route when the link appears on screen. To navigate in code, use useRouter in Client Components.

server-component.definition: A component that runs only on the server: it can be async, access the database and secrets directly, and its code is not sent to the browser. It cannot use state, effects or events. It is the default in the App Router.

client-component.definition: A component marked with "use client" at the top of the file, which also runs in the browser and can use state, effects, events and browser APIs. It and everything it imports go into the JavaScript sent to the client; that is why it should stay at the leaves of the tree.

ssr.definition: Page generation strategies. SSG builds the HTML at build time (fast, ideal for fixed content); SSR builds it on every request (always fresh data, more server cost); ISR is SSG that regenerates after a while or on demand, without a new build. In today's Next, these ideas show up as static or dynamic routes, cached content and partial prerendering, which mixes static and dynamic parts on the same page.

hidratacao.definition: The step in which React, in the browser, attaches events and state to the HTML that came ready from the server. If the server HTML differs from what the client renders (dates, Math.random, window), a hydration error occurs.

use-client.title: Server and Client together
use-client.body: The page fetches data on the server and passes it to an interactive button, which is the only part sent as JavaScript to the browser.

server-action.definition: An async function marked with "use server" that runs on the server and can be called straight from a form or a Client Component, without creating an API route. Since it is a public endpoint under the hood, it must validate input and check permissions.

route-handler.definition: A route.js file inside app/ that exports functions named after HTTP methods (GET, POST...) and creates an API endpoint. Used for webhooks, integrations and clients other than the app itself.

streaming.definition: The server sends the page in pieces: what is ready appears right away, and slow sections, wrapped in <Suspense>, arrive later with a fallback in their place. It improves time to first content without waiting for the slowest query.

route-handler-exemplo.title: GET and POST endpoint
route-handler-exemplo.body: Each exported function handles one method. Response.json builds the response with the status.

server-action-form.title: Form with a Server Action
server-action-form.body: The form works even without JavaScript in the browser. The action validates, saves and revalidates the list.

ssr-vs-ssg.question: When should you use SSR, SSG or ISR?
ssr-vs-ssg.answer: SSG for content that is the same for every user and barely changes over time (docs, landing pages): it is the fastest. ISR when the content is the same for everyone but changes sometimes (catalog, blog): static with revalidation. SSR when it depends on the request (logged-in user, cookies) or must always be current. In today's Next I think in parts of the page: what is the same for everyone stays static or cached, and what depends on the request stays dynamic, inside Suspense.

server-vs-client.question: What is the difference between Server and Client Components?
server-vs-client.answer: Server Components run only on the server: they fetch data directly, send no JavaScript to the browser and have no state or events. Client Components ("use client") also run in the browser and allow interactivity. I keep the page as a Server Component and mark only the interactive pieces as client, to ship less JavaScript.

erro-hidratacao.question: What causes a hydration error and how do you fix it?
erro-hidratacao.answer: The HTML rendered on the server differing from the first render in the browser. Common causes: dates and times (a different time zone), random values, reading window or localStorage during render, and invalid HTML (a div inside a p). I fix it by generating the value only on the client inside a useEffect, loading the component without SSR, or ensuring the same data on both sides.

server-action-seguranca.question: Are Server Actions secure by default?
server-action-seguranca.answer: No. Under the hood, each action is a POST endpoint that anyone can call with any data. Inside it I validate the input (Zod), check the session and the user's permission on the resource, and do not trust ids hidden in the form. Next.js protects against CSRF by checking the origin, but authorization is my responsibility.

por-que-nextjs.question: What does Next.js add to React?
por-que-nextjs.answer: File-based routing, server rendering (SSR, SSG, ISR and streaming), Server Components, Server Actions and API routes, image and font optimization, automatic code splitting per route and a production-ready build, with Turbopack as the default bundler. With plain React, each of these pieces is a separate choice and setup.

route-handler-vs-action.question: When should you use a Route Handler and when a Server Action?
route-handler-vs-action.answer: A Server Action for mutations triggered by the app itself (forms, buttons), because it integrates with revalidation and works without writing fetch. A Route Handler when the endpoint is consumed from outside: webhooks, mobile apps, integrations, or when I need to control the method, headers and response format.

proxy.definition: Code that runs before the request reaches the route, defined in a proxy.ts file at the root, with export function proxy and a matcher that picks the routes. It is used to redirect, rewrite URLs, do lightweight authentication checks and adjust headers. In Next 16 it replaced middleware.ts, now deprecated (the middleware-to-proxy codemod does the switch), and it runs on Node.js; anyone who still needs the edge runtime keeps middleware.ts.

cache-e-revalidacao.title: Caching and revalidation
cache-e-revalidacao.body: With cacheComponents enabled (Next 16), whatever can be reused gets 'use cache', with cacheLife for the duration and cacheTag to invalidate it later with updateTag. Without cacheComponents, the previous model applies, with revalidate and no-store on each fetch and revalidatePath. The details are in the Next.js performance track.
